behavioral_effects: A backend 4xx now reaches the browser with the backend's own message. Proved live against the running backend: POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm with an invalid token returned {detail: 'Backend API error: 401 Unauthorized'} from the pre-change container on :3000 and {detail: 'Reset link is invalid or has expired'} from a source-backed Next dev server on :3100.
Request validation failures surface FastAPI's per-field messages joined with '; ' instead of 'Backend API error: 422 Unprocessable Entity'. Proved live on POST /api/contact with an invalid body.
5xx keeps the caller's generic message and ignores the backend body, so proxy handlers cannot leak internal detail on an unexpected server error.

auth/login, auth/register and auth/oauth-callback dropped their hand-rolled extraction for the shared helper. register gains the domain-message branch it never had, so an AlreadyExistsError on signup now shows 'Email already registered' rather than 'Registration failed'.
compatibility_impact: None. The proxy response contract is unchanged: still {detail: string} at the same HTTP status, which is exactly what api-client.ts reads at frontend/src/lib/api-client.ts:108. Only the content of the string changes, so no caller needs updating.
follow_up: About 73 catch blocks under frontend/src/app/api still repeat the same four-line shape (instanceof BackendApiError -> NextResponse.json, else a generic 500). A proxyErrorResponse(error, fallback) helper returning the whole response would delete roughly 280 lines. Left out here because it is a second reason and this envelope is one reason per session.
limitations: No browser or Playwright run. The chain was verified at the HTTP boundary with curl through a source-backed Next dev server talking to the real running backend, so the proxy hop is proved end to end but toast rendering itself was not exercised.

The motivating MCP 409 was not reproduced directly because it needs an authenticated session. It is covered by proving the identical AppException envelope path on password-reset/confirm, plus a unit test that uses the 409 body verbatim.
The dev stack on port 3000 is a built container image and keeps serving the pre-change behaviour until it is rebuilt.
reason: Proxy handlers returned BackendApiError.message ('Backend API error: 409 Conflict') and discarded the parsed backend body held in .data, so every domain error message the backend worded for the user - e.g. 'MCP connection with this name already exists' on a duplicate Integrations connect - reached the browser toast as a bare HTTP status line. The handlers now forward the backend's error.message, while 5xx stays generic so internal detail is not leaked.
risks: Any 4xx message the backend adds in future is now user-visible wherever a proxy handler surfaces it. Today's messages are all deliberately user-facing, but a future domain exception that embeds internal detail in a 4xx message would reach the browser without a second gate.
rollback: git revert restores previous behaviour completely; no migration, persisted state, or configuration is involved. Note a revert also restores the three hand-rolled body extractions in auth/login, auth/register and auth/oauth-callback, including the missing domain-message branch in register.
security_impact: Reduces leak surface rather than widening it. The helper discards the response body entirely for status >= 500, so an unexpected server error cannot carry internal detail into a browser toast; previously auth/login and auth/oauth-callback surfaced the backend body at any status including 5xx. Making 4xx domain messages user-visible is the point of the change, and those strings are already worded for end users by the domain layer; the four raw HTTPException details in the backend are likewise user-facing ('File not found', OAuth error text).
summary: Surface the backend's structured error message through the Next.js proxy handlers instead of the generic BackendApiError status line
